title: 20-layer HfO2/SiO2 alternating stack with fine-tuned thicknesses for UV-reflection/SWIR-transmission
scientific_hypothesis: An alternating HfO2/SiO2 multilayer stack with individually optimized thicknesses can produce a spectral response that reflects 200-400 nm while transmitting 800-1500 nm, with the optimal solution lying in a narrow manifold around thicknesses that produced 0.8206 target score in prior iterations.
design_principle: Recalled knowledge: Alternating high/low index dielectric layers create constructive interference for reflection at certain wavelengths. By adjusting individual layer thicknesses away from strict quarter-wave values, the reflection band can be positioned in the UV while maintaining transmission in the SWIR. The stack acts as a distributed Bragg reflector for UV but becomes increasingly transparent at longer wavelengths where optical thicknesses are smaller relative to wavelength.
proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (20 layers total, alternating starting with HfO2)
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 20 layers, seeded from the 0.8206-score thickness vector [30.0, 40.0, 30.0, 40.0, 31.0, 40.0, 31.0, 40.0, 30.0, 40.0, 49.0, 40.0, 50.0, 40.0, 49.0, 40.0, 50.0, 40.0, 49.0, 40.0] nm, with perturbation bounds ±0.6 nm
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 800-1500 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 200-400 nm band
Maintain smooth spectral transitions between bands
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 20 (within 30-layer limit)
All thicknesses in practical deposition range (30-50 nm)
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave stacks produce high reflection at design wavelength; deviating from quarter-wave shifts the reflection band
Recalled knowledge: HfO2 has higher refractive index than SiO2 in visible-SWIR range, creating index contrast for interference effects
Recalled knowledge: UV wavelengths are shorter, so thinner layers can still produce constructive interference for reflection
Recalled knowledge: At longer wavelengths (SWIR), the same physical thicknesses represent smaller optical thicknesses, reducing reflection and increasing transmission
expected_advantages: Starting from proven high-scoring thickness vector reduces search space
Narrow perturbation bounds (±0.6 nm) focus exploration on local optimum rather than global search
Constrained optimization prevents degradation below 0.02 of running best score
20 layers provides sufficient degrees of freedom while staying well under 30-layer limit
known_risks: Uncertain whether the 0.8206-score solution is a local or global optimum - narrower bounds may trap search in local maximum
Recalled refractive index dispersion of HfO2 and SiO2 in UV (200-400 nm) may differ from actual catalog data - extinction coefficients in UV could affect performance
The alternating pattern may not be optimal; a different sequence could perform better but this route does not explore sequence changes
Manufacturing tolerance on thin layers (30 nm) may be challenging; actual deposition variation could shift spectral response
What would settle these: measured n/k dispersion data from material catalog, tolerance sensitivity analysis, alternative sequence testing in a separate route
execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer planar multilayer dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Materials: alternating hfo2 and SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) layers, starting with hfo2 adjacent to air. Layer sequence: hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), hfo2, SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) (20 layers total). Initialize thicknesses at [30.0, 40.0, 30.0, 40.0, 31.0, 40.0, 31.0, 40.0, 30.0, 40.0, 49.0, 40.0, 50.0, 40.0, 49.0, 40.0, 50.0, 40.0, 49.0, 40.0] nm. Optimize all 20 thicknesses with perturbation bounds ±0.6 nm around current best. Apply penalty if target score drops more than 0.02 below running best. Wavelength bands: maximize reflectance in 200-400 nm, maximize transmittance in 800-1500 nm. Normal incidence, unpolarized light. Total layers must equal exactly 20.
revision_reason: Refinement based on prior iteration results: seeding from 0.8206 target score thickness vector, reducing perturbation bounds from ±1.5 nm to ±0.6 nm to constrain search within proven optimal manifold, adding constrained optimization mode that penalizes score drops >0.02 relative to running best
